第 49 章 Leading Through Rapid Change Is Normal带领团队经历快速变化是常态

Yvette Pasqua / 伊薇特·帕斯夸

— 第 144 页 —

Do you feel like you're constantly leading your team through one change after another? Have you wondered when it's going to end so that you can get back to your "normal" job of managing teams to ship software? Well, the truth is: the change is not going to end.

你是否觉得自己在不断带领团队经历一个又一个变化？你有没有想过这什么时候结束，好让你回到管理团队交付软件的「正常」工作？事实是：变化不会结束。

As managers in the tech industry, we need to lead our teams through constant, rapid change, whether it's technical, cultural, or business change. Our growth industry requires us to be comfortable with high ambiguity and rate of change. We need to be able to solve problems, inspire, and motivate teams with positivity during change. This is challenging, often thankless work, that doesn't show up in performance reviews or Objectives and Key Results (OKRs). There's rarely training, so what can we do?

作为科技行业的经理，我们需要带领团队经历持续快速的变化，无论是技术、文化还是业务变化。我们的增长行业要求我们适应高度模糊和变化速度。我们需要在变化中用积极态度解决问题、激励团队。这是有挑战、通常不讨好的工作，不会出现在绩效评估或 OKR 中。很少有培训，那我们能做什么？

Here's a framework to help you lead teams through change. It has two components: Time phase (Where is the company at in the change timeline?) and Leadership qualities (What type of leadership does the company need?).

这里有一个框架帮你带领团队经历变化。它有两个组成部分：时间阶段（公司在变化时间线的哪里？）和领导品质（公司需要什么类型的领导？）。

Time Phase时间阶段

There are three time phases that require different things from leaders:

有三个时间阶段，对领导有不同要求：

— 第 145 页 —

Acute phase. The month or two following an event that typically triggers rapid change (because there almost always is one), such as hiring a new CTO, an acquisition, or closing a round of funding.

急性期。典型触发快速变化的事件（因为几乎总有一个）之后的一两个月，比如新 CTO 入职、收购、或完成一轮融资。

Rapid phase. The next and longest phase lasts several months. It is the period of predictably constant, rapid change. If you plot time on the x-axis and the number of changes on the y-axis, you see constant change growth.

快速期。下一个也是最长的阶段持续几个月。它是可预测的持续快速变化时期。如果你把时间画在 x 轴、变化数量画在 y 轴，你看到持续的变化增长。

New normal. When constant change begins to decelerate and plateau. In our growth industry, this means you've reached a (temporary) "new" normal.

新常态。当持续变化开始减速并趋于平稳。在我们的增长行业，这意味着你达到了一个（暂时的）「新」常态。

Leadership Qualities领导品质

There are three leadership qualities that are most important when leading through change: communication, motivation, and focus. We need to optimize for them differently depending on the time phase we're in and what our company needs from us as leaders.

带领团队经历变化时三个最重要的领导品质是：沟通、激励和专注。我们需要根据所处时间阶段和公司作为领导对我们的需要，对它们做不同优化。

— 第 146 页 —

Communication. Managers need to overcommunicate during times of change and optimize for the exact balance of these methods:

沟通。经理在变化时期需要过度沟通，优化以下方法的精确平衡：

  • Use one-way (i.e., presentations) and two-way (i.e., small group Q&A) communications strategically策略性地使用单向（即演讲）和双向（即小组问答）沟通
  • Use the proper mix of both written and in-person communications恰当混合书面和面对面沟通
  • Be as transparent as you can尽可能透明
  • Provide enough context about why change is happening提供足够的关于为什么变化正在发生的上下文
  • Actively listen and communicate in an empathetic way积极倾听并以共情方式沟通

Motivation. It's essential that managers keep teams highly motivated through rapid change. You can use these practices:

激励。经理让团队在快速变化中保持高动力至关重要。你可以用这些做法：

  • Paint a picture of a company and software product that inspires everyone描绘一幅激励每个人的公司和软件产品图景
  • Emphasize company values to ground the team强调公司价值观让团队扎根
  • Make sure everyone understands the company vision, mission, and strategy确保每个人理解公司愿景、使命和战略
  • Manage with the appropriate balance of empowerment versus direction because it will change用授权与指导的适当平衡来管理，因为它会变
  • Help your teams set clear goals so that they can measure their impact帮团队设定清晰目标以便他们衡量影响
— 第 147 页 —

Focus. It's so easy to lose focus during growth and change. Don't let it happen! Push yourself to do the following:

专注。在增长和变化中很容易失去专注。别让它发生！逼自己做以下事情：

  • Invest in only the most important initiatives even when it's easy to invest in more只投资最重要的计划，即使很容易投资更多
  • Continue to improve your ability to execute and deliver持续提升执行和交付能力
  • Become great at regularly prioritizing and reprioritizing the work擅长定期对工作排优先级和重新排优先级

You can use this framework by thinking of a time of change you faced or are facing, and for each time phase, write down the leadership qualities that are most valuable for your company's specific situation. Doing this exercise as a retrospective can really help you learn from the past and come up with actionable things to try to do better next time. Doing this exercise as you're experiencing change can help you prioritize and organize your time so that you can lead your team positively through it.

你可以用这个框架想想你面对过或正在面对的变化时期，为每个时间阶段写下对你公司具体情况最有价值的领导品质。作为回顾做这个练习真的能帮你从过去学习、想出下次尝试做得更好的可行动事项。在经历变化时做这个练习可以帮你排优先级和组织时间，让你能积极带领团队度过。

For example, using this framework I did a retrospective of the year after my company was acquired and learned the following:

例如，用这个框架我对公司被收购后那一年做了回顾，学到了以下：

Acute phase: It's important to over-index on in-person, two-way, communication over other methods. I didn't see trust rebuild with my team until I did small group meetings with a lot of Q&A. In those, I could be transparent and provide nuanced context, and they could see I was really empathetic and listening to their concerns.

急性期：过度强调面对面双向沟通比其他方式重要。直到我做了很多问答的小组会议，我才看到和团队的信任重建。在那些会议中，我可以透明、提供细致的上下文，他们可以看到我真的在共情和倾听他们的担忧。

Rapid phase: We needed to periodically reset to the proper balance of empowerment versus direction in order to keep our cross-functional teams motivated and focused. As the company grew and changed, that balance frequently changed in different ways and we didn't reset it often enough.

快速期：我们需要定期重置授权与指导的适当平衡，以保持跨职能团队的动力和专注。随着公司增长和变化，那个平衡经常以不同方式变化，我们没有足够频繁地重置。

New normal: A focus on execution and delivery of our key initiatives was critical, as was regularly prioritizing only the key initiatives. It's far too easy to become distracted.

新常态：聚焦于关键计划的执行和交付至关重要，定期只对关键计划排优先级也一样。分心太容易了。
